title: RAW UNREVIEWED: Vitruvius crown assay preserves equal mass while comparing displaced water
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_TESTED. Vitruvius narrates equal-weight gold, silver and crown trials in a refilled vessel; the crown displaces more water than the gold comparator. Equal mass is preserved across three objects; immersion couples each object to displaced water, a restored starting level makes measurements comparable, and unequal water loss is used to infer altered composition. No balance-in-water procedure or numeric alloy fraction is supplied by these paragraphs.

design.contrast: Weight-only purity treats a matching delivered mass as sufficient. Appearance-only purity treats workmanship as sufficient. A cumulative-immersion rival changes the vessel baseline and cannot preserve the reported comparison.
design.prediction: A full reading must keep equal weight compatible with unequal displacement, carry the crown identity across both tests, and distinguish replacement water from the weighed metal. It must not infer the source explicitly reports crown displacement below silver; that comparison is not written here.
